svg.title: Where new code belongs in the storefront repo
svg.desc: A decision tree routing a new type to one of five folders, based on whether it performs I/O, whether it is an entry point, whether it encodes a business rule, and whether more than one service needs it.

span.p: Does it talk to anything outside the process?

span.p: Is it an entry point we expose?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Does it encode a business rule?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: web/ - one handler plus its request and response types

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: infra/ - one adapter per outside system

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: domain/ - pure types and functions, imports nothing of ours

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Do two or more services need it today?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: platform/ - shared kernel, needs review from both teams

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: app/ - orchestration inside the one service that needs it
